Death Reference No.1 of 1985 
with Criminal Appeal No. 93 of 1985 with

lawyer:
S.A. Hasan. A.A.G. with Sajjad Ali Chowdhury. A.A.G.  -------- For the State. 
Md. Shahjahan, Advocate -------- For the Condemned Prisoner Hazrat Ali (appointed by the State) 
Mujibor Rahman, Advocate -------- For the Condemned Prisoner Abdur Rahman.
parties:
Hazrat Ali & Abdur Rahman -------- Condemned Prisoner & Appellant.
Vs.
The State -------- Respondent.
full_judgment: 40. In the absence of any positive material to the contrary the presumption of correctness of recording the confessional statement upon observing all formalities can very well be inferred and we have reason to believe that P.W.9 and P.W. 12 on being satisfied that the accused would freely and voluntarily confess their guilt, recorded their confession and that the accused also made no complaint before the Magistrate, We do not find any cogent reason as to why self implication of the appellants in the commission of offence can not be taken as true. Retraction of confession at an earliest opportunity sometime may lend support to the defence plea that the confession was not voluntary one but for the belated retraction of a confession as in the present case without any material to support it, no such inference can be drawn. Rather, the consensus of judicial decisions are that an accused may be convicted even on a retracted confession, if it is inculpatory and found to be voluntary and true. It has been further contended that prolonged police custody immediately proceeding the confession is sufficient, if not properly explained, to find the confession as involuntary. In the case of Abdur Rouf and others Vs. The State reported in 38 DLR 197 the delay in producing the accused before the magistrate from the police custody was ignored and it is held, in the absence of any positive material to the contrary, the presumption of correctness of recording the confessional statement upon observing all formalities may very well be inferred. In the present case mere keeping the appellant in police custody for 3 days does not ipso facto make the confession involuntary in nature. We are satisfied that all the required legal formalities have been observed in the case by the Magistrate in recording e confession. There is nothing on record to show that the accused persons made the confession out of fear or torture or maltreatment of the police and or that the confession was the result of inducement. We have already noted that the learned Magistrate recorded the confessional statement in respect of both the condemned prisoners after giving sufficient caution to them and gave them reasonable time for reflection of their mind. The learned Magistrate also was satisfied that the confessions are voluntarily made by the two condemned prisoners. The contents of the confessional statements of the condemned prisoners Hazrat Ali and Abdur Rahman gave a ring of truth when the statements are mingled with other evidence on record and attending circumstances. The statements of the two condemned prisoners not only corroborated each other, the discovery of the dead bodies in pursuance of the statement and at the instance of the condemned prisoner Hazrat Ali and bringing out of the spade by accused Abdur Rahman and the presence of nylon thread around the neck of the dead bodies having been corroborated by other oral and circumstantial evidence lead us to believe that confessional statements of the condemned prisoners arc voluntary and true as well. The confession of the two convicts voluntarily made coupled with the circumstantial evidence has furnished the link in the chain of evidence and they are so consistently established that no other inference but the guilt of the appellants Hazrat Ali and Abdur Rahman can be the only conclusion. The defence theory of innocence of the accused persons has been ruled out as being improbable. The attending circumstances are highly against the condemned prisoners. The accused Hazrat Ali was found by P.W. Dipchand and P.W.Dr. Golamuddin after the occurrence at a place which is far away from his place of residence. The recovery of the dead bodies in pursuance of his statement made to the police, presence of nylon rope on the necks of the dead bodies are the corroborative elements to the confession on some particulars. Thus the confession of the accused appellants receives ample corroboration from independent circumstantial evidence on material points. So far as the two condemned prisoners Hazrat Ali and Abdur Rahman are concerned we have already observed that by making voluntary and true statements in their confession they admitted their participation in the commission of the alleged murder of Sapan Kumar Mitra and Mashiur Rahman. On careful consideration of the evidence and materials on record we hold that the prosecution had satisfactorily proved by inculpatory confessional statement and attending circumstances that condemned prisoner Hazrat Ali and Abdur Rahman did commit the murder intentionally in furtherance of common intention of both and they took the dead bodies by truck and buried them at Boalgari with a view to screening the offence and they have rightly been found guilty and as such convicted by the learned trial Court under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code along with secs. 201/34 of the Penal Code.
